'''Mary Grace Kovar''' (July 6, 1929 – September 21, 2015){{r|fg|sad}} was an American statistician.

Kovar worked as chief of the Analytical Coordination Branch of the Division of Analysis at the [[National Center for Health Statistics]].

For many years she was the coordinator of ''Health, United States'', a series of books reporting the health statistics of Americans.{{r|duffy}}
By 1996, she had retired from the NCHS,{{r|sad}} and had become a senior research scientist at [[NORC at the University of Chicago]].{{r|n96}}
She was a vice president at NORC by 2000.{{r|n00}}

She married Earl S. Pollack, a [[biostatistics|biostatistician]] at the [[National Institutes of Health]]. Pollack died in 2012.{{r|pollack}}

The topics of some of Kovar's best-cited publications include trends in [[blood lead level]]s,{{ran|A}}
[[infant nutrition]] and its effects on health,{{ran|B}}
patterns of sensitivity to [[allergen]]s,{{ran|C}},
[[longitudinal study|longitudinal studies]] of [[aging]],{{ran|D}}
and a comparison of the results of in-person interviews versus telephone surveys.{{ran|E}}

Kovar was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 1979, seven years after Pollack.{{r|fasa}} She became a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 1990.{{r|aaas}}
